rounds.text: Interarch Building Solutions faces significant concerns regarding its cash generation, as evidenced by a negative operating cash flow of Rs -19 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -138 Cr in Mar 2026 [E29, E30]. This disconnect is highlighted by a poor cash conversion ratio of -0.14x, with operating cash flow representing only 15% of reported profit [E28, E31]. The stock is currently struggling with negative momentum, trading well below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages and sitting near the bottom of its 52-week range [E44, E42]. Institutional confidence appears to be waning, as evidenced by a reduction in holdings by both foreign and domestic institutions since Sep 2024 [E36, E37]. Furthermore, the company trades at a premium valuation compared to its sector, with a P/B ratio of 3.31x against a sector benchmark of 1.34x [E7]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with minimal debt [E32, E53], and has demonstrated robust historical profit growth [E17, E54]. Despite these strengths, the inconsistent operating margin trends and the significant capital expenditure build-up in CWIP suggest that future profitability remains subject to execution risk [E26, E27, E34].
